The Most High said: ﴿My Lord, grant me wisdom and join me with the righteous.﴾ ﴿And grant me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations.﴾ ﴿And make me among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss.﴾ ﴿And forgive my father, for he was among the misguided.﴾ ﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected,﴾ ﴿the Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, ﴾ ﴿except one who comes to God with a sound heart.﴾

Know that when God the Most High related Abraham's praise of God, peace be upon him, He then mentioned his supplication and his request. This is an alert that placing praise before supplication is of great importance. The verification of this matter is that these human souls are of the same kind as the angels. Whenever their occupation with the knowledge of God the Most High, His love, and their attraction to the world of spirituality is more intense, their resemblance to the angels is more complete, and so they become stronger in exercising influence over the bodies of this world. And whenever their occupation with the pleasures of this world and their immersion in the darknesses of these corporeal things is more intense, their resemblance to the beasts is greater, and so they become more incapable, weaker, and less influential in this world. Therefore, whoever wishes to occupy himself with supplication must precede it with the praise of God the Most High and the mention of His greatness and majesty, to the extent that through that remembrance he becomes absorbed in the knowledge and love of God and comes to resemble the angels closely. Through that resemblance he attains a divine, heavenly power, and so he becomes the source of the occurrence of that thing which is the object of the supplication. This is the uncovering of the reality of supplication, and it becomes clear that placing praise before supplication is obligatory. Through this, the verification of his words, peace be upon him, is manifested, relating from God the Most High: "Whoever is so occupied with remembering Me that he does not ask Me, I shall give him the best of what I give to those who ask."

This is what is meant by his saying ﴿and join me with the righteous﴾. As for the external ones: they are wealth and status. Wealth is more corporeal, and status is more spiritual. So Abraham, peace be upon him, left the corporeal matter, which is wealth, and requested the spiritual matter, which is status and a good remembrance that remains throughout time. The answer: The intention is not to praise the disbeliever as a disbeliever, but rather that he be praised by every person and beloved in every heart.

The third request: his saying: ﴿And make me among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss.﴾ Know that when he requested the happiness of this world, he then requested the happiness of the Hereafter, which is the Garden of Bliss. He described it with inheritance, because inheritance is what is gained in this world. So he likened the spoils of the Hereafter to the spoils of this world.

The fourth request: his saying: ﴿And forgive my father, for he was among the misguided.﴾ Know that when he finished requesting the worldly and otherworldly happinesses for himself, he requested them for the person most closely attached to him, which is his father. This view is weak, because praying on this condition is permissible for a disbeliever, so if his supplication were conditional, God would not have forbidden him from it.

The first: His saying ﴿and do not disgrace me﴾ indicates that nothing is obligatory upon God the Most High, as we explained in His saying: ﴿and the One from whom I hope He will forgive my sin on the Day of Judgment﴾.

Second: the one who says, when he first said, "And make me among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss" (Q. 26:85), and once Paradise is attained, disgrace is impossible; so how did he say afterward, "And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected" (Q. 26:87)? Third: The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) said: in [yub'athun] (they are resurrected), the pronoun refers either to the servants, because it is known, or to the misguided (ḍāllīn).

As for His saying, "except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart" (Q. 26:89): know that the Exalted honored him with this attribute when He said, "And indeed, among his followers was Abraham. When he came to his Lord with a sound heart" (Q. 37:83–84).

Then in this exception there are several aspects:

The first: when it is said to you, "Does Zayd have wealth and sons?" you say, "His wealth and sons are the soundness of his heart," intending the negation of wealth and sons from him and the affirmation of soundness of heart for him in their place. So likewise in this verse.

The second: that we take the speech according to its meaning and make wealth and sons into the sense of richness, as if it were said: "The Day when neither richness will benefit, except the richness of one who comes to Allah with a sound heart," because a man's richness in his religion is by the soundness of his heart, just as his richness in his worldly life is by his wealth and his sons.

The third: that we make [man] (whoever) the object of "yanfa'u" (benefits), meaning: no wealth and no sons will benefit except a man whose heart was sound along with his wealth, in that he spent it in obedience to Allah the Exalted, and along with his sons, in that he guided them to the religion. It is also permissible, on this reading, that "except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart" be from the trial of wealth and sons.

As for "sound" (salīm), there are three interpretations:

The first, and it is the most correct, is that what is meant by it is the soundness of the heart from ignorance and vile character traits. This is because just as the health and soundness of the body is an expression for the presence of what is appropriate in its temperament, composition and connections, and its sickness is an expression for the loss of one of those matters, so likewise the soundness of the heart is an expression for the presence of what is appropriate for it, which is knowledge and noble character, and its sickness is an expression for the loss of one of these two. So His saying, "except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart," means one who is free of corrupt beliefs and inclination toward the desires and pleasures of this world. If it is said: the apparent meaning of this verse requires that whoever's heart is sound is saved, and that there is no need for soundness of tongue and hand. The answer: the heart is the influential factor, while the tongue and limbs follow it; so if the heart were sound, they would necessarily be sound too. Since they are not sound, it is established that the heart is not sound.

The second interpretation: the sound (salīm) is the one stung (ladīgh) by the fear of Allah the Exalted.

The third interpretation: the sound is the one who was safe (salima), submitted (aslama), made peace (sālama), and yielded (istaslama). And Allah knows best.

The second discussion: concerning the matters he requested in the supplication, which are several requests.

And from his saying ﴿and join me with the righteous﴾ is meant the perfection of the practical faculty, which is by being one who acts with good. For the perfection of a human being is that he knows the Truth for its own sake and the good for the sake of acting upon it. Also, it is possible for him to know the Truth without knowing the good, but the reverse is not possible. The second request: Since it has been established that what is meant by ḥukm is knowledge, it is established that he, peace be upon him, asked God to give him knowledge of God the Most High and His attributes. His saying ﴿and join me with the righteous﴾ indicates that the servant being righteous is only by the creation of God the Most High. So if we directed the supplication toward it, that would be a request for attaining what is already attained, which is invalid.

* * *

The third request: The wisdom sought in the supplication is either the knowledge of God or of something other than Him, and the second is false. Then, that knowledge is either the knowledge of God the Most High that is the condition for the validity of faith, or something other than it. And if it were already attained by him, requesting its attainment would be impossible. The second request: his saying: ﴿And grant me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations.﴾ On this there are three interpretations:

The first interpretation: He, peace be upon him, began by asking for what is the essential perfection of a human being in this world and the Hereafter, which is the request for ḥukm, that is knowledge. The internal ones: outward form and inward form. The outward form is more corporeal, and the inward form is more spiritual. This is what is meant by his saying ﴿and join me with the righteous﴾. As for the external ones: they are wealth and status. Wealth is more corporeal, and status is more spiritual. So Abraham, peace be upon him, left the corporeal matter, which is wealth, and requested the spiritual matter, which is status and a good remembrance that remains throughout time. Some objected to this, saying that the desire to praise a disbeliever is not appropriate. The answer: The intention is not to praise the disbeliever as a disbeliever, but rather that he be praised by every person and beloved in every heart.

The third request: his saying: ﴿And make me among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss.﴾ Know that when he requested the happiness of this world, he then requested the happiness of the Hereafter, which is the Garden of Bliss. He described it with inheritance, because inheritance is what is gained in this world. So he likened the spoils of the Hereafter to the spoils of this world.

The fourth request: his saying: ﴿And forgive my father, for he was among the misguided.﴾ Know that when he finished requesting the worldly and otherworldly happinesses for himself, he requested them for the person most closely attached to him, which is his father. So he said: ﴿And forgive my father.﴾ Then on this there are several points:

First: Forgiveness is conditioned upon Islam, and requesting the conditioned thing implies requesting the condition. So his saying ﴿and forgive my father﴾ amounts in its meaning to a supplication for his father to attain Islam.

Second: His father had promised him Islam, as God the Most High said: ﴿And Abraham's seeking forgiveness for his father was only due to a promise he had made to him﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:114], so he prayed for him on this condition. Praying for a disbeliever on this condition is not prohibited. ﴿But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:114]. This view is weak, because praying on this condition is permissible for a disbeliever, so if his supplication were conditional, God would not have forbidden him from it.

Third: His father had told him that he was privately upon his religion but outwardly upon the religion of Nimrod out of taqiyyah (dissimulation for fear of harm), so he prayed for him, believing the matter to be as stated. When the contrary became clear to him, he disassociated himself from him. Therefore he said in his supplication: ﴿for he was among the misguided.﴾ Had he not believed that his father was not misguided at the time, he would not have said that.

The fifth request: his saying: ﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected.﴾ The author of al-Kashshaf said: "Ikhzā' (disgracing) is from khizy, which is humiliation, or from khazāyah, which is shame." Here there are some investigations:

The first: His saying ﴿and do not disgrace me﴾ indicates that nothing is obligatory upon God the Most High, as we explained in His saying: ﴿and the One from whom I hope He will forgive my sin on the Day of Judgment﴾.

Second: the one who says, when he first said, "And make me among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss" (Q. 26:85), and once Paradise is attained, disgrace is impossible; so how did he say afterward, "And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected" (Q. 26:87)? Also, Allah the Exalted said, "Indeed, disgrace this Day and evil are upon the disbelievers" (Q. 16:27). So if it is the portion of the disbelievers alone, how would the infallible one fear it? The answer: just as the good deeds of the righteous are the bad deeds of those brought near (to Allah), so likewise the ranks of the righteous are the lower levels of those brought near, and the disgrace of each one is according to what befits him.

Third: The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) said: in [yub'athun] (they are resurrected), the pronoun refers either to the servants, because it is known, or to the misguided (ḍāllīn).

First: It is not permissible to interpret ḥukm (wisdom, judgment) as prophethood, because prophethood was already attained. Rather, what is meant by ḥukm is the perfection of the theoretical faculty, which is through the apprehension of the Truth. And from his saying ﴿and join me with the righteous﴾ is meant the perfection of the practical faculty, which is by being one who acts with good. For the perfection of a human being is that he knows the Truth for its own sake and the good for the sake of acting upon it. He placed his saying ﴿My Lord, grant me ḥukm﴾ before his saying ﴿and join me with the righteous﴾ because the theoretical faculty takes precedence over the practical faculty in both nobility and essence. Also, it is possible for him to know the Truth without knowing the good, but the reverse is not possible. Also, because knowledge is an attribute of the soul and action is an attribute of the body, and since the soul is nobler than the body, knowledge is superior to action. We have explained the knowledge of things as ḥukm because a human being does not know the realities of things unless he brings into his mind the images of their quiddities, then attributes some of them to others by negation or affirmation. That attribution is ḥukm. Then, if the mental attributions correspond to the external attributions, the mental attributions become impossible to change, and so they become firm and strong. Such apprehension is called ḥikmah (wisdom) and ḥukm, and this is what is meant by his, peace be upon him, saying: "Show us things as they truly are." As for ṣalāḥ (righteousness), it is the rational faculty being in the middle between the two vices of excess and deficiency, because excess on one side is deficiency on the other side and vice versa. So righteousness is not attained except through moderation. Since true moderation is one thing that does not admit division at all, and human thoughts in this world are limited to apprehending such things, there is no escape for humans from departing from that limit, however slightly. But the departure of those brought near (to God) from it occurs in such a small degree that it is not perceived, while the departure of the disobedient from it is extremely gross. From this, the verification of what has been said becomes clear: "The good deeds of the righteous are the sins of those brought near." And it becomes clear why Abraham, peace be upon him, needed to say: ﴿and join me with the righteous﴾.

The second request: Since it has been established that what is meant by ḥukm is knowledge, it is established that he, peace be upon him, asked God to give him knowledge of God the Most High and His attributes. This indicates that the knowledge of God the Most High does not come into the heart of the servant except by the creation of God the Most High. His saying ﴿and join me with the righteous﴾ indicates that the servant being righteous is only by the creation of God the Most High. To interpret these things as lutf (divine grace that facilitates obedience) is far-fetched, because according to the opponent, whatever lutf is within God's power, He has already done it. So if we directed the supplication toward it, that would be a request for attaining what is already attained, which is invalid.

* * *

The third request: The wisdom sought in the supplication is either the knowledge of God or of something other than Him, and the second is false. This is because a person, while he is occupied with the knowledge of one thing, cannot simultaneously be occupied with the knowledge of another thing. So if the object of this supplication were knowledge of other than God the Most High, and knowledge of other than God is a hindrance to being absorbed in the knowledge of God, then this request would be a request for something that would preoccupy him from being absorbed in the knowledge of God the Most High. That is impermissible, because there is no perfection beyond that absorption. Therefore, the object of this supplication is the knowledge of God. Then, that knowledge is either the knowledge of God the Most High that is the condition for the validity of faith, or something other than it. The first is false, because since it must be attained by all believers, how could it not be attained by Abraham, peace be upon him? And if it were already attained by him, requesting its attainment would be impossible. Thus it is established that the object of this supplication is degrees in the knowledge of God the Most High beyond knowledge of His existence, that He is not spatially bounded, nor does He inhere in what is spatially bounded, and that He is an All-Powerful, Living, Knowing Being. And that is nothing but attaining (the knowledge of) the attributes of majesty, or attaining the knowledge of the reality of the Essence, or the manifestation of the light of that knowledge in the heart. [p. 129] Beyond this there are states that speech cannot express and imagination cannot describe, and whoever wishes to reach them must be among those who arrive at the Essence (itself), not among those who merely hear reports.

The second request: his saying: ﴿And grant me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations.﴾ On this there are three interpretations:

The first interpretation: He, peace be upon him, began by asking for what is the essential perfection of a human being in this world and the Hereafter, which is the request for ḥukm, that is knowledge. Then after that he asked for the perfections of this world, and after that the perfections of the Hereafter. As for the perfections of this world, some are internal and some are external. The internal ones: outward form and inward form. The outward form is more corporeal, and the inward form is more spiritual. So Abraham, peace be upon him, left the corporeal matter, which is the outward form, and requested the spiritual matter, which is the inward form. This is what is meant by his saying ﴿and join me with the righteous﴾. As for the external ones: they are wealth and status. Wealth is more corporeal, and status is more spiritual. So Abraham, peace be upon him, left the corporeal matter, which is wealth, and requested the spiritual matter, which is status and a good remembrance that remains throughout time. This is what is meant by his saying ﴿and grant me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: God gave him that through His saying: ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt 37:108].

The first, in the language of wisdom: We have explained that human souls have influence in general, but some of them may be weak and thus incapable of influence. When a group of them gathers, their collective strength may achieve what individuals could not. This meaning is observed in corporeal influences. Given this, when a single person is such that a great multitude praises him, honors him, and exalts him, the turning of their aspirations toward him when they gather may become a cause for an increase in his perfection.

The second, in the language of perfection: Whoever becomes praised among people because of the virtues he possesses, that praise and that fame become a motive for others to acquire similar virtues.

The second interpretation: He asked his Lord to make among his descendants at the end of time one who would call to God the Most High, and that is Muhammad ﷺ. Thus what is meant by his saying ﴿and grant me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations﴾ is the mission of Muhammad ﷺ.

The third interpretation: Some said: What is meant is the agreement of the adherents of all religions upon loving him. God the Most High then granted him that, because you do not see any religion's adherents except that they revere Abraham, peace be upon him. Some objected to this, saying that the desire to praise a disbeliever is not appropriate. The answer: The intention is not to praise the disbeliever as a disbeliever, but rather that he be praised by every person and beloved in every heart.

The third request: his saying: ﴿And make me among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss.﴾ Know that when he requested the happiness of this world, he then requested the happiness of the Hereafter, which is the Garden of Bliss. He described it with inheritance, because inheritance is what is gained in this world. So he likened the spoils of the Hereafter to the spoils of this world.

The fourth request: his saying: ﴿And forgive my father, for he was among the misguided.﴾ Know that when he finished requesting the worldly and otherworldly happinesses for himself, he requested them for the person most closely attached to him, which is his father. So he said: ﴿And forgive my father.﴾ Then on this there are several points:

First: Forgiveness is conditioned upon Islam, and requesting the conditioned thing implies requesting the condition. So his saying ﴿and forgive my father﴾ amounts in its meaning to a supplication for his father to attain Islam.

Second: His father had promised him Islam, as God the Most High said: ﴿And Abraham's seeking forgiveness for his father was only due to a promise he had made to him﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:114], so he prayed for him on this condition. Praying for a disbeliever on this condition is not prohibited. ﴿But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:114]. This view is weak, because praying on this condition is permissible for a disbeliever, so if his supplication were conditional, God would not have forbidden him from it.

Third: His father had told him that he was privately upon his religion but outwardly upon the religion of Nimrod out of taqiyyah (dissimulation for fear of harm), so he prayed for him, believing the matter to be as stated. When the contrary became clear to him, he disassociated himself from him. Therefore he said in his supplication: ﴿for he was among the misguided.﴾ Had he not believed that his father was not misguided at the time, he would not have said that.

The fifth request: his saying: ﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected.﴾ The author of al-Kashshaf said: "Ikhzā' (disgracing) is from khizy, which is humiliation, or from khazāyah, which is shame." Here there are some investigations:

The first: His saying ﴿and do not disgrace me﴾ indicates that nothing is obligatory upon God the Most High, as we explained in His saying: ﴿and the One from whom I hope He will forgive my sin on the Day of Judgment﴾.

Third: The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) said: in [yub'athun] (they are resurrected), the pronoun refers either to the servants, because it is known, or to the misguided (ḍāllīn).

The second interpretation: the sound (salīm) is the one stung (ladīgh) by the fear of Allah the Exalted.

The third interpretation: the sound is the one who was safe (salima), submitted (aslama), made peace (sālama), and yielded (istaslama). And Allah knows best.

The Most High said: ﴿My Lord, grant me wisdom and join me with the righteous.﴾ ﴿And grant me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations.﴾ ﴿And make me among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss.﴾ ﴿And forgive my father, for he was among the misguided.﴾ ﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected,﴾ ﴿the Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, ﴾ ﴿except one who comes to God with a sound heart.﴾

Know that when God the Most High related Abraham's praise of God, peace be upon him, He then mentioned his supplication and his request. This is an alert that placing praise before supplication is of great importance. The verification of this matter is that these human souls are of the same kind as the angels. Whenever their occupation with the knowledge of God the Most High, His love, and their attraction to the world of spirituality is more intense, their resemblance to the angels is more complete, and so they become stronger in exercising influence over the bodies of this world. And whenever their occupation with the pleasures of this world and their immersion in the darknesses of these corporeal things is more intense, their resemblance to the beasts is greater, and so they become more incapable, weaker, and less influential in this world. Therefore, whoever wishes to occupy himself with supplication must precede it with the praise of God the Most High and the mention of His greatness and majesty, to the extent that through that remembrance he becomes absorbed in the knowledge and love of God and comes to resemble the angels closely. Through that resemblance he attains a divine, heavenly power, and so he becomes the source of the occurrence of that thing which is the object of the supplication. This is the uncovering of the reality of supplication, and it becomes clear that placing praise before supplication is obligatory. Through this, the verification of his words, peace be upon him, is manifested, relating from God the Most High: "Whoever is so occupied with remembering Me that he does not ask Me, I shall give him the best of what I give to those who ask."

If someone says: Why did Abraham, peace be upon him, not restrict himself to praise, especially since it is also narrated from him that he said: "My asking is sufficed by His knowledge of my state"? The answer: He, peace be upon him, only mentioned that while he was occupied with calling the people to the Truth. Do you not see that he said: ﴿For they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds﴾, and then he mentioned praise, and then he mentioned supplication? This is because the lawgiver necessarily must teach the Law. As for when he was alone with himself, and his purpose was not to teach the Law, he would restrict himself to his saying: "My asking is sufficed by His knowledge of my state."

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 26, verses 102–104:**

[Verses 90–104 of Surah al-Shu'ara' are quoted here in full.]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near for the righteous﴾ ﴿and Hellfire will be made apparent for the deviators﴾ ﴿and it will be said to them, "Where is that which you used to worship﴾ ﴿besides Allah? The second: His saying: ﴿And it will be said to them, "Where is that which you used to worship"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and the hosts of Iblis, all together.﴾ The meaning is: Where are your gods? Do they benefit you by helping you, or do they benefit themselves by defending themselves? For they and their gods are fuel for the Fire. This is His saying: ﴿So they will be thrown into it, they and the deviators﴾, that is, the gods and their worshippers, to whom the Hellfire has been made apparent. The third: His saying: ﴿They will say while they dispute therein:﴾ ﴿"By Allah, we were in manifest error,﴾ ﴿when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds."﴾

Know that the apparent meaning of this is that whoever worshipped disputes with the one worshipped and addresses him with these words. Yet the state of the idols is one of two possibilities. Either Allah creates them in the Hereafter as lifeless objects with which He punishes the people of the Fire, in which case they cannot be addressed, and His saying ﴿when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds﴾ must be understood as not being addressed to them. Or it is said that He brings them back to life in the Fire, but this too is not permissible, because they bear no sin for having been worshipped by others. The closest view, then, is that they said this when they saw the images of the idols, as an acknowledgment of their great error and out of remorse, not as direct address. What is to be understood as genuine address is their saying: ﴿And none has led us astray except the criminals,﴾ and by it they meant those among the jinn and mankind who called them to worship idols. This is like their saying: ﴿Our Lord, we obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they led us astray from the way﴾ [al-Ahzab: 67].

As for their saying: ﴿So we have no intercessors,﴾ as we see the believers having intercessors among the angels and the prophets, ﴿nor a close friend﴾, as we see the believers having friends, because no one is a true friend in the Hereafter except the believers, while among the people of the Fire there is enmity and hatred. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67]. Alternatively, ﴿So we have no intercessors, nor a close friend, ḥamīm﴾ means: from among those whom we used to count as intercessors and friends, because they used to believe that their idols were their intercessors with Allah the Exalted, and they had friends among the devils of mankind. Or they meant that if they fell into destruction, they knew that intercessors and friends would neither benefit them nor ward off harm from them. So by denying them they intended to deny whatever benefit was attached to them, because what does not benefit is judged as nonexistent. Ḥamīm comes from al-iḥtimām (concern), which is the one who cares about what concerns you. Or it comes from al-ḥāmmah, meaning the select, and means the pure friend. The reason intercessors is plural while friend is singular is that intercessors are customarily many, whereas friends are few. A man afflicted with the oppression of a tyrant may have a large group of the people of his town rise to intercede for him out of compassion, but as for a friend, meaning one sincere in his affection for you, he is rarer than the eggs of the male raven (a proverb for rarity). It is also permissible that by "friend" he means the plural.

Then Allah the Exalted related their saying: ﴿So if only we had another return, we would be among the believers,﴾ and that they wished to return to the world. The word law (لَوْ, "if") in such a context carries the sense of tamannī (wishing), as if it were said: "So if only we had a return." This is because of the convergence in meaning between law (لَوْ) and layta (لَيْتَ, "if only") in estimation. It is also permissible that law remains in its original sense and its answer is omitted, the answer being "we would have done such and such."

Al-Jubba'i said: Their saying ﴿then we would be among the believers﴾ is not a report about their faith, but a report about their resolve, because if it were a report about their faith it would have to be true, since lying does not occur among the people of the Hereafter. Yet Allah the Exalted has reported the opposite in His saying: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. The corruption of this statement has already been explained in Surah al-An'am.

Then He, glory be to Him, made clear that in what He mentioned of the story of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) there is a sign for whoever wishes to take guidance from it. Then He said: ﴿but most of them were not believers.﴾ Most of the exegetes understood this as referring to the people of Ibrahim. Then Allah the Exalted made clear that despite all these proofs, most of his people did not believe in him. Thus this is a consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ) regarding the denial his own people showed him.

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful,﴾ its meaning is that He is able to hasten retribution, but He is merciful in granting respite so that they may believe.

**The Third Story: The Story of Noah (peace be upon him)**

﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers.﴾ ﴿When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not be mindful of God?"﴾ ﴿Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿They said, "Shall we believe you, when the lowest of people follow you?"﴾ ﴿He said, "What is my knowledge of what they used to do?"﴾ ﴿Their reckoning is only upon my Lord, if you could perceive.﴾ ﴿I am not one to drive away the believers.﴾ ﴿I am only a clear warner.﴾ ﴿They said, "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned."﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me."﴾ ﴿So decide between me and them with a decision, and save me and those believers who are with me.﴾ ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ .

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers.﴾ ﴿When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not be mindful of God?"﴾ ﴿Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿They said, "Shall we believe you, when the lowest of people follow you?"﴾ ﴿He said, "What is my knowledge of what they used to do?"﴾ ﴿Their reckoning is only upon my Lord, if you could perceive.﴾ ﴿I am not one to drive away the believers.﴾ ﴿I am only a clear warner.﴾ ﴿They said, "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned."﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me."﴾ ﴿So decide between me and them with a decision, and save me and those believers who are with me.﴾ ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ .

Know that when God, exalted is He, related to Muhammad (ﷺ) the account of Moses and Abraham as a consolation to him for what he encountered from his people, He also related to him the account of Noah (peace be upon him). His account was greater than the accounts of others, because he called his people for a thousand years less fifty years, and despite that, his people denied him. So He said: ﴿The people of Noah denied﴾. He said "kadhdhabat" (denied, feminine) because the word "qawm" (people) is feminine, and its diminutive is "quwaymah." He related of them that they denied the messengers for two reasons:

The first: even though they denied Noah, his denial in meaning includes the denial of others, because the way of recognizing the messengers does not differ. Therefore, in meaning, He related of them that they denied the messengers.

The second: the people of Noah denied all of God's messengers, either because they were of the *zanadiqa* (heretics) or of the *Barahima* (Brahmins).

* * *

As for His saying, ﴿their brother﴾, it is because he was one of them. It is like the saying of the Arabs, "O brother of the Banu Tamim," meaning "O one of them" (*yā akhā Banī Tamīm*, in Arabic). Then, He, glorified is He, related of Noah (peace be upon him) that first he warned them, and second that he described himself. As for the warning, it is his saying: ﴿Will you not be mindful of God?﴾

Know that the people only accepted those religions by *taqlid* (blind imitation), and the one who imitates, when warned, fears. What has not produced fear in his heart does not occupy itself with reasoning. For this reason, he placed before all his words His saying: ﴿Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ As for his description of himself, it was by two matters:

The first: his saying, ﴿Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ This is because he was known among them for trustworthiness, as Muhammad (ﷺ) was among the Quraysh. It is as if he said: "I was trustworthy before, so how do you accuse me today?"

The second: his saying, ﴿I do not ask you for any reward for it﴾, that is, for what I am engaged in of claiming prophethood, lest it be supposed of him that he called them out of desire (for gain). If it is said: why did he repeat the command to be mindful? The answer: in the first, he meant ﴿Will you not be mindful of my opposition, while I am God's messenger?﴾ and in the second: ﴿Will you not be mindful of my opposition, while I take no reward from you?" So the meaning is different and there is no repetition in it. A man may say to another: "Will you not be mindful of God regarding my disobedience, though I raised you as a child?" and "Will you not be mindful of God regarding my disobedience, though I taught you when you were grown?"

He placed the command to be mindful of God, exalted is He, before the command to obey Him, because being mindful of God is the cause of obeying Him, so he placed the cause before the effect. Then, when Noah (peace be upon him) said that to them, they answered him with their saying: ﴿Shall we believe you, when the lowest of people follow you?﴾

The author of *al-Kashshaf* said: It was read "wa-atbā‘uka al-arḏalūn" (*wa-atbā‘uka*, with *atbā‘* as the plural), which is the plural of *tābi‘* like *shāhid* and *ashhād*, or the plural of *tabaʿ* like *baṭal* and *abṭāl*. The *wāw* is for the circumstantial clause, and its proper form is that *qad* be implied after it in ﴿wa-ittaba‘aka﴾. *Arḏal* is pluralized both regularly and irregularly, in their saying: ﴿those who are our lowest﴾ [Hud: 27]. *Radhāla* means baseness. They looked down on them only because of their lowly lineage and their scant share of worldly goods. It was also said that they were of the lowly crafts, such as weaving and cupping.

Know that this objection is extremely feeble, because Noah (peace be upon him) was sent to all creation, so the situation does not differ in that by reason of poverty, wealth, the nobility or baseness of livelihoods. Noah (peace be upon him) answered them with the true answer, which is his saying: ﴿What is my knowledge of what they used to do?﴾ This statement indicates that they, along with that, attributed to them that they had not believed out of reflection and insight, but had believed out of desire and greed, as God, exalted is He, related of them in His saying: ﴿those who are our lowest, at first glance﴾ [Hud: 27]. Then He said: ﴿Their reckoning is only upon my Lord﴾, meaning: we consider only the outward of their affairs, not what is hidden. **The fourth story: the story of Hud, peace be upon him**

Their sayings: "The people of 'Ad denied the messengers. When their brother Hud said to them, 'Will you not fear God? Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you. So fear God and obey me. I ask you for no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds. Do you build on every high place a landmark, sporting? And you take fortresses, perhaps you will abide forever. And when you strike, you strike as tyrants. So fear God and obey me. And fear Him who has provided you with what you know: He has provided you with livestock and children, and gardens and springs. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day.' They said, 'It is the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers. This is only the custom of the earlier people, and we will not be punished.' So they denied him, and We destroyed them. Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers. And indeed, your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful."

God Most High says: "The people of 'Ad denied the messengers..." (the passage is repeated in full, as above).

Know that the opening of this story and the opening of the story of Noah, peace be upon him, are one, so there is no benefit in repeating the commentary. Then God Most High mentions the matters about which Hud, peace be upon him, spoke with them, and they are three.

The first is His saying: "Do you build on every high place a landmark, sporting?" The word *rī'* (high place) has been read with a kasra and with a fatha. It means an elevated place, and from it comes the saying "How high is your land?" (*kam rai'u ardika*), meaning its height. The word *āya* means a landmark. Then there are several views on this:

First, from Ibn 'Abbas: they used to build a landmark on every high place, sporting with those who passed along the road to Hud, peace be upon him.

Second, they used to build in elevated places so that their wealth would be known through it, out of boasting, so they were forbidden from this and were described as sporting.

He did so, and the she-camel came out and knelt down before them, and there came forth from her a young one like her in size. Salih, peace be upon him, charged them with two matters:

He did so, and the she-camel came out and knelt down before them, and there came forth from her a young one like her in size. Salih, peace be upon him, charged them with two matters:

The first: his saying: ﴿for her is a share of water, and for you is a share of a known day.﴾ Qatada said: when it was her day of drinking, she would drink all their water, and their drinking was on the day she did not drink.

The second: his saying: ﴿And do not touch her with harm﴾, that is, by striking, or hamstringing, or otherwise, ﴿lest the punishment of a tremendous day seize you.﴾ He magnified the day because the punishment descends in it, and describing the day with it is more emphatic than describing the punishment, for when a time is magnified because of what happens in it, its effect is all the more intense in magnitude. Then God, exalted is He, related of them that they hamstrung her. It is narrated that Mis'ada drove her to a narrow place and shot her with an arrow so that she fell; then Qudar struck her.

The first: the *musaḥḥar* is one who has been bewitched greatly, until it overcame his intellect.

The second: ﴿of the bewitched﴾ means one who has *siḥr* (a belly/throat); every creature that eats is *musaḥḥara*, and *siḥr* is the upper belly. It is related from al-Farrā': the *musaḥḥar* is one who has a stomach, meaning you eat food and drink drink.

The third: from al-Mu'arrij: the *musaḥḥar* is the created being, in the dialect of Bajīla.

The second of their responses: their saying: ﴿You are only a human like us, so bring a sign, if you are among the truthful.﴾ This admits of two matters:

The first: that you are a human like us, so how can you be a prophet? This is in the same vein as what they used to say about prophets, that if they were truthful, they would be of the kind of the angels.

The second: that their intent was: you are a human like us, so for establishing your prophethood we need a proof. Then Salih, peace be upon him, said: ﴿This is a she-camel; for her is a share of water.﴾ It is also read with a ḍamma. It is narrated that they said: "We want a pregnant she-camel to come out of this rock and give birth to a young camel." So Salih sat pondering, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to him: "Pray two units and ask your Lord for the she-camel."

Page 138
He did so, and the she-camel came out and knelt down before them, and there came forth from her a young one like her in size. Salih, peace be upon him, charged them with two matters:

The first: his saying: ﴿for her is a share of water, and for you is a share of a known day.﴾ Qatada said: when it was her day of drinking, she would drink all their water, and their drinking was on the day she did not drink.

The second: his saying: ﴿And do not touch her with harm﴾, that is, by striking, or hamstringing, or otherwise, ﴿lest the punishment of a tremendous day seize you.﴾ He magnified the day because the punishment descends in it, and describing the day with it is more emphatic than describing the punishment, for when a time is magnified because of what happens in it, its effect is all the more intense in magnitude. Then God, exalted is He, related of them that they hamstrung her. It is narrated that Mis'ada drove her to a narrow place and shot her with an arrow so that she fell; then Qudar struck her.

If it is asked: why did the punishment seize them when they had repented?

The answer has two aspects:

The first: their remorse was not the remorse of penitents, but the remorse of those fearing the imminent punishment.

The second: that the remorse, even if it was the remorse of penitents, occurred at a time other than the time of repentance, rather at the moment of witnessing the punishment. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds﴾ [al-Nisa': 18], and so on. The definite article in "the punishment" points to the punishment of a tremendous day.

The sixth story: the story of Lot, peace be upon him.

﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers.﴾ ﴿When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear God?"﴾ ﴿Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ ﴿So fear God and obey me.﴾ ﴿And I do not ask you any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds?﴾ ﴿And you leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a people who transgress.﴾ ﴿They said, "If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be among those expelled."﴾ ﴿He said, "Indeed, I am of those who detest your deed."﴾ ﴿"My Lord, save me and my family from what they do."﴾ ﴿So We saved him and his family, all of them,﴾ ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind.﴾ ﴿Then We destroyed the others.﴾ ﴿And We rained upon them a rain, and wretched was the rain of those who were warned.﴾ ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers.﴾ ﴿When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear God?"﴾ ﴿Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ ﴿So fear God and obey me.﴾ ﴿And I do not ask you any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds?﴾ ﴿And you leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a people who transgress.﴾ ﴿They said, "If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be among those expelled."﴾ ﴿He said, "Indeed, I am of those who detest your deed."﴾ ﴿"My Lord, save me and my family from what they do."﴾ ﴿So We saved him and his family, all of them,﴾ ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind.﴾ ﴿Then We destroyed the others.﴾ ﴿And We rained upon them a rain, and wretched was the rain of those who were warned.﴾ ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful.﴾

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds?﴾, it is possible that the phrase refers back to the verb "approach" (ta'tūn), meaning: you are among the worlds, and you have become singled out by this attribute, which is approaching males. It is also possible that it refers back to the object of the approach (al-ma'tiyy), meaning: you have chosen males from among the worlds, not females from among them.

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿from among your spouses﴾ (min azwājikum), it is suitable that it be an explanation (tabyīn) of "what He created" (mā khalaqa), and it is also suitable that it be partitive (lil-tab'īḍ, "of"). By "what He created" is meant the permitted part of them (the wives). It seems that they used to do the same with their women. The ʿādī (transgressor) is the one who exceeds in his wrongdoing. The meaning is: Do you commit this sin despite its enormity? ﴿Rather, you are a people who transgress﴾ in all sins, so this is included in that, or it means: rather, you are a people deserving to be described as transgressors, since you committed such an abomination.

Then they said to him, peace be upon him: ﴿If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be among those expelled.﴾ That is, you will surely be among those whom we expel from our land. Perhaps they used to expel those whom they expelled in the worst conditions. Then Lot, peace be upon him, said to them: ﴿Indeed, I am of those who detest your deed.﴾ Al-qilā (detestation) is intense hatred, as if it is a hatred that burns the heart and the liver. His saying: ﴿of those who detest﴾ (min al-qālīn) is more emphatic than saying "I am one who detests your deed" (innī li-ʿamalikum qālin), just as one says "So-and-so is among the scholars," which is more emphatic than your saying "So-and-so is a scholar." It is also permissible that it means: of those who are the most complete in their detestation of you.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So We saved him and his family﴾, and the meaning is: We saved him and his family from the punishment of their deed.

﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind.﴾ If it is said: "among those who remained behind" (fī al-ghābirīn) is a description of her, as if it were said "except an old woman who remained behind," but remaining behind was not her attribute at the time of their deliverance.

The answer: its meaning is "except an old woman whose remaining behind was decreed." It was said that she perished along with those who remained behind from the town, by what was rained upon them of stones.

Al-Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Jabbār said in his Tafsīr, regarding His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses﴾, that it is evidence for the invalidity of determinism (al-jabr) from several aspects:

The first: it is not said "you leave" (tadharūn) except with the capacity to do otherwise. For this reason one does not say to a person, "Why do you leave ascending to the sky?" as one says to him, "Why do you leave entering and exiting?"

The second: He said: ﴿what He created for you﴾, and if the creation of the act belonged to God, the one created for them would be what He created in them and decreed, not what they did not do.

The third: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Rather, you are a people who transgress﴾. If God created in them what they did, how are they attributed to transgression? Is it said to the black person, "You are a transgressor in your color"?

We say: the sum of these aspects returns to the fact that if the servant did not originate the acts of his own self, praise, blame, command and prohibition would not be directed at him. This verse, in this meaning, has a special feature beyond what occurred of command, prohibition, praise and blame in the story of Moses, Abraham, Noah and the rest of the stories. So why did he restrict this story to these aspects and not the rest of the stories?

When the invalidity of these aspects is established, that well-known aspect remains. We answer it with the two well-known responses:

The first: when God, may He be exalted, knew the occurrence of these things, their non-existence is impossible, because their non-existence would entail the reversal of knowledge into ignorance, which is impossible; and what leads to the impossible is impossible. When their non-existence is impossible, imposing the obligation of abstaining is imposing the impossible.

The second: when the capable one is capable of two opposites, it is impossible for one of the two objects of capacity to be preferred over the other except by a preponderant factor, which is the motive or the will. That preponderant factor is originated, so it has an effector. If that effector is the servant, an infinite regress (tasalsul) follows, which is impossible. If the effector is God, the Exalted, then that is compulsion (jabr) according to your view. Thus, by these two decisive proofs, what he said is shown to be untenable. And God knows best.

**The Seventh Story: the story of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him)**

﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers. When Shu'ayb said to them, "Will you not be mindful of God? I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So be mindful of God and obey me. I ask of you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds. Give full measure and do not be among the cheaters. And weigh with a true balance. And do not deprive people of their due, and do not spread corruption on earth, causing mischief. And fear Him who created you and the former generations." They said, "You are only one of the bewitched. You are only a human like us, and we think you are surely among the liars. So make pieces of the sky fall upon us, if you are among the truthful." He said, "My Lord knows best what you do." But they denied him, so the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. It was indeed the punishment of a tremendous day. Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And surely your Lord, He is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾

The statement of the Exalted: ﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers. When Shu'ayb said to them, "Will you not be mindful of God? I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So be mindful of God and obey me. I ask of you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds. Give full measure and do not be among the cheaters. And weigh with a true balance. And do not deprive people of their due, and do not spread corruption on earth, causing mischief. And fear Him who created you and the former generations." They said, "You are only one of the bewitched. You are only a human like us, and we think you are surely among the liars. So make pieces of the sky fall upon us, if you are among the truthful." He said, "My Lord knows best what you do." But they denied him, so the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. It was indeed the punishment of a tremendous day. Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And surely your Lord, He is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾

The word ﴿the companions of the Thicket﴾ (ʼaṣḥāb al-ʼayka) has been read with the hamza, with the hamza eased, and in the genitive (bi-l-jarr) as an idafa (construction of possession), and this is the preferred reading. As for one who reads it in the accusative and claims that Ayka is, in the pattern of Layla, the name of a town known by that name, this is a delusion led to by the script of the Mushaf, since it is found written in this surah and in Surat Sad without an alif. However, it has been written in the rest of the Qur'an in its original form, and the story is one. Moreover, Ayka is a name that is not known. It is narrated that the companions of the Thicket were people of dense trees, and those trees were the ones whose fruit is the doum palm (al-muqul). If it is said: why did he not say "their brother Shu'ayb," as in the other passages? The answer: Shu'ayb was not one of the companions of the Thicket. In a hadith: "Indeed Shu'ayb, brother of Madyan, was sent to them and to the companions of the Thicket."

Then Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) commanded them in several matters:

The first of them is His saying: ﴿Give full measure and do not be among the cheaters.﴾ This is because measuring has three kinds: full, short (taṭfīf), and excessive. So he commanded the obligatory, which is giving full measure, with His saying ﴿Give full measure﴾, and he forbade the prohibited, which is short measure (taṭfīf), with His saying ﴿and do not be among the cheaters﴾. He did not mention the excessive, because if one does it, he has done good, and if he does not do it, there is no sin upon him. Then, when he commanded giving full measure, he explained how to do it, saying: ﴿And weigh with a true balance.﴾ It has been read as al-qisṭās with a damma and with a kasra, and it means the balance (al-mīzān). It is also said to be al-qarasṭūn.

The second: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not deprive people of their due.﴾ It is said: bakhasahu ḥaqqahu, when one diminishes it for him. This is general for every right that belongs to someone, that it must not be encroached upon, and for every property, that its owner must not be usurped, nor may it be disposed of except with his permission, in a lawful manner.

The third: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not spread corruption on earth, causing mischief.﴾ It is said: ʻathā fī al-arḍ, ʻathiya, and ʻāʻa, and this is like cutting the road, raiding, and destroying crops. They used to do that together with their practice of various kinds of corruption, so they were forbidden from that.

The fourth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And fear Him who created you and the former generations.﴾ It has been read as al-Jubulla (with a ḍamma on the jīm, in the pattern of al-Ubulla), and read as al-Jibla (in the pattern of al-Khilqa). Their meaning is one, that is, those of the creation (dhawī al-jibilla). The intent is that He is the One who bestowed favor by creating them and creating those who preceded them, from whom, had it not been for their creation, they would not have been created.

[Page 141]

So the people had no answer except what, had they left it, would have been more fitting for them. And it is of two aspects:

The first: their saying: ﴿You are only one of the bewitched﴾ and ﴿You are only a human like us.﴾ If it is said: did the meaning differ by including the conjunction (wāw) here and omitting it in the story of Thamud? The answer: when the wāw is included, two meanings are intended, both contrary to prophethood in their view: magic and humanness. When the wāw is omitted, they intended only one meaning, which is that he is bewitched; then they established it by his being a human like them.

The second: their saying: ﴿and we think you are surely among the liars.﴾ Its meaning is clear. Then Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) used to threaten them with punishment if they persisted in denial, so they said: ﴿So make pieces of the sky fall upon us.﴾ It has been read as kisfan with sukūn and with a vowel, and both are the plural of kisfa, which is a piece. And the sky (al-samāʼ) is the cloud or the canopy (al-ẓulla). They only asked for that because they deemed its occurrence unlikely, so they thought that if it did not happen, his lie would be shown. Thereupon Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) said: ﴿My Lord knows best what you do.﴾ He did not invoke a curse upon them, but entrusted the matter to God, exalted is He. When they persisted in denial, God sent down upon them the punishment that they had demanded, the punishment of the Day of the Canopy, if by "the sky" they meant the cloud. And if they meant the canopy, then He diverted from them what they had demanded. It is narrated that He withheld the wind from them for seven days and sent upon them sand, which took their breath; neither shade nor water benefited them. So they were compelled to go out into the desert, and a cloud shaded them. They found in it coolness and a breeze, so they gathered beneath it, and it rained fire upon them, and they were burned. It is also narrated that Shu'ayb was sent to two nations, the people of Madyan and the companions of the Thicket. Madyan was destroyed by the cry of Jibril (peace be upon him), and the companions of the Thicket by the punishment of the Day of the Canopy.

Here ends the discussion of these seven stories that God, exalted is He, mentioned in this surah, as consolation for Muhammad (ﷺ) for the severe grief he suffered. Two questions remain here:

The first question: Why is it not permissible to say that the punishment that descended upon ʻĀd, Thamūd, the people of Lūṭ, and others was not because of their disbelief and obstinacy, but because of the conjunctions of the stars (qirānāt al-kawākib) and their connections, as the astrologers (ahl al-nujūm) agreed? And if this possibility stands, the lesson of these stories is not attained, because the lesson is attained only if we know that the descent of this punishment was because of their disbelief and obstinacy.

The second: God, exalted is He, may send down punishment as a trial (miḥna) for the responsible people and a test for them, as He said: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and who are patient﴾ [Muhammad: 31]. And because He, exalted is He, has tested the believers with great affliction in many places, and when that is so, the descent of affliction upon them does not indicate that they were in falsehood. The answer: God, exalted is He, sent down these stories upon Muhammad (ﷺ) as consolation and to remove grief from his heart. When God, exalted is He, informed Muhammad that He is the One who sent down the punishment upon them, and that He sent it upon them only as a recompense for their disbelief, that is informing Muhammad (ﷺ) that the matter is so. Then consolation and joy come to him (peace be upon him) by it.

Some people argued against the validity of the science of judgments (ʻilm al-aḥkām, astrological prediction) by saying: the influence in these things is either the stars, or the zodiac signs (burūj), or the star's being in a specific sign (burj). The first is invalid; otherwise these effects would occur wherever the star is. The second is also invalid; otherwise the effect would last as long as the sign lasts. The third is also invalid, because the celestial sphere (falak), according to their view, is simple, not composite, so the nature of each sign is equal to the nature of the other sign in complete quiddity. Thus the state of the star while in its sign is like its state while in another sign, and it would follow that this effect would persist as long as the star persists. The people (who hold the view) may say: why is it not permissible that the emergence of the effect from the specific star is contingent on its being in a particular alignment (musāmata makhṣūsa) with another star, so that when that alignment is lost, the condition of influence is lost, and so influence does not occur? And they may say: this proof only shows that they are not influential by their essences and natures, but it does not show that they are not influential by the course of custom (jary al-ʻāda). So when God, exalted is He, makes His custom to produce specific effects following the connections, conjunctions, and cycles of the stars, it does not follow from the occurrence of these effects that God, exalted is He, created them for the purpose of deterring the disbelievers. Rather, perhaps He, exalted is He, created them as a repetition of those customs. And God knows best.

Here ends the discussion of these seven stories that God, exalted is He, mentioned in this surah, as consolation for Muhammad (ﷺ) for the severe grief he suffered. Two questions remain here:

The first question: Why is it not permissible to say that the punishment that descended upon ʻĀd, Thamūd, the people of Lūṭ, and others was not because of their disbelief and obstinacy, but because of the conjunctions of the stars (qirānāt al-kawākib) and their connections, as the astrologers (ahl al-nujūm) agreed? And if this possibility stands, the lesson of these stories is not attained, because the lesson is attained only if we know that the descent of this punishment was because of their disbelief and obstinacy.

The second: God, exalted is He, may send down punishment as a trial (miḥna) for the responsible people and a test for them, as He said: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and who are patient﴾ [Muhammad: 31]. The answer: God, exalted is He, sent down these stories upon Muhammad (ﷺ) as consolation and to remove grief from his heart. When God, exalted is He, informed Muhammad that He is the One who sent down the punishment upon them, and that He sent it upon them only as a recompense for their disbelief, that is informing Muhammad (ﷺ) that the matter is so. Then consolation and joy come to him (peace be upon him) by it.

Some people argued against the validity of the science of judgments (ʻilm al-aḥkām, astrological prediction) by saying: the influence in these things is either the stars, or the zodiac signs (burūj), or the star's being in a specific sign (burj). The first is invalid; otherwise these effects would occur wherever the star is. The second is also invalid; otherwise the effect would last as long as the sign lasts. The third is also invalid, because the celestial sphere (falak), according to their view, is simple, not composite, so the nature of each sign is equal to the nature of the other sign in complete quiddity. Thus the state of the star while in its sign is like its state while in another sign, and it would follow that this effect would persist as long as the star persists. The people (who hold the view) may say: why is it not permissible that the emergence of the effect from the specific star is contingent on its being in a particular alignment (musāmata makhṣūsa) with another star, so that when that alignment is lost, the condition of influence is lost, and so influence does not occur? So when God, exalted is He, makes His custom to produce specific effects following the connections, conjunctions, and cycles of the stars, it does not follow from the occurrence of these effects that God, exalted is He, created them for the purpose of deterring the disbelievers. Rather, perhaps He, exalted is He, created them as a repetition of those customs. And God knows best.

Then, when he commanded giving full measure, he explained how to do it, saying: ﴿And weigh with a true balance.﴾ It has been read as al-qisṭās with a damma and with a kasra, and it means the balance (al-mīzān). It is also said to be al-qarasṭūn.

This is general for every right that belongs to someone, that it must not be encroached upon, and for every property, that its owner must not be usurped, nor may it be disposed of except with his permission, in a lawful manner.

Their meaning is one, that is, those of the creation (dhawī al-jibilla). The first: their saying: ﴿You are only one of the bewitched﴾ and ﴿You are only a human like us.﴾ If it is said: did the meaning differ by including the conjunction (wāw) here and omitting it in the story of Thamud? They said, "You are only one of the bewitched. You are only a human like us, and we think you are surely among the liars. So make pieces of the sky fall upon us, if you are among the truthful." He said, "My Lord knows best what you do." But they denied him, so the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. It was indeed the punishment of a tremendous day. Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And surely your Lord, He is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾

However, it has been written in the rest of the Qur'an in its original form, and the story is one. Moreover, Ayka is a name that is not known. So he commanded the obligatory, which is giving full measure, with His saying ﴿Give full measure﴾, and he forbade the prohibited, which is short measure (taṭfīf), with His saying ﴿and do not be among the cheaters﴾. He did not mention the excessive, because if one does it, he has done good, and if he does not do it, there is no sin upon him. Then, when he commanded giving full measure, he explained how to do it, saying: ﴿And weigh with a true balance.﴾ It has been read as al-qisṭās with a damma and with a kasra, and it means the balance (al-mīzān). It is also said to be al-qarasṭūn.

This is general for every right that belongs to someone, that it must not be encroached upon, and for every property, that its owner must not be usurped, nor may it be disposed of except with his permission, in a lawful manner.

The third: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not spread corruption on earth, causing mischief.﴾ It is said: ʻathā fī al-arḍ, ʻathiya, and ʻāʻa, and this is like cutting the road, raiding, and destroying crops. **The Seventh Story: the story of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him)**

﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers. When Shu'ayb said to them, "Will you not be mindful of God? I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So be mindful of God and obey me. I ask of you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds. Give full measure and do not be among the cheaters. And weigh with a true balance. And do not deprive people of their due, and do not spread corruption on earth, causing mischief. And fear Him who created you and the former generations." They said, "You are only one of the bewitched. You are only a human like us, and we think you are surely among the liars. So make pieces of the sky fall upon us, if you are among the truthful." He said, "My Lord knows best what you do." But they denied him, so the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. It was indeed the punishment of a tremendous day. Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And surely your Lord, He is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾

The statement of the Exalted: ﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers. When Shu'ayb said to them, "Will you not be mindful of God? I am to you a trustworthy messenger. The word ﴿the companions of the Thicket﴾ (ʼaṣḥāb al-ʼayka) has been read with the hamza, with the hamza eased, and in the genitive (bi-l-jarr) as an idafa (construction of possession), and this is the preferred reading. As for one who reads it in the accusative and claims that Ayka is, in the pattern of Layla, the name of a town known by that name, this is a delusion led to by the script of the Mushaf, since it is found written in this surah and in Surat Sad without an alif. However, it has been written in the rest of the Qur'an in its original form, and the story is one. Moreover, Ayka is a name that is not known. It is narrated that the companions of the Thicket were people of dense trees, and those trees were the ones whose fruit is the doum palm (al-muqul). The first of them is His saying: ﴿Give full measure and do not be among the cheaters.﴾ This is because measuring has three kinds: full, short (taṭfīf), and excessive. So he commanded the obligatory, which is giving full measure, with His saying ﴿Give full measure﴾, and he forbade the prohibited, which is short measure (taṭfīf), with His saying ﴿and do not be among the cheaters﴾. He did not mention the excessive, because if one does it, he has done good, and if he does not do it, there is no sin upon him. Then, when he commanded giving full measure, he explained how to do it, saying: ﴿And weigh with a true balance.﴾ It has been read as al-qisṭās with a damma and with a kasra, and it means the balance (al-mīzān). It is also said to be al-qarasṭūn.

The second: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not deprive people of their due.﴾ It is said: bakhasahu ḥaqqahu, when one diminishes it for him. This is general for every right that belongs to someone, that it must not be encroached upon, and for every property, that its owner must not be usurped, nor may it be disposed of except with his permission, in a lawful manner.

The third: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not spread corruption on earth, causing mischief.﴾ It is said: ʻathā fī al-arḍ, ʻathiya, and ʻāʻa, and this is like cutting the road, raiding, and destroying crops. Here ends the discussion of these seven stories that God, exalted is He, mentioned in this surah, as consolation for Muhammad (ﷺ) for the severe grief he suffered. Two questions remain here:

Thus the state of the star while in its sign is like its state while in another sign, and it would follow that this effect would persist as long as the star persists. Then consolation and joy come to him (peace be upon him) by it.

Some people argued against the validity of the science of judgments (ʻilm al-aḥkām, astrological prediction) by saying: the influence in these things is either the stars, or the zodiac signs (burūj), or the star's being in a specific sign (burj). Rather, perhaps He, exalted is He, created them as a repetition of those customs. And God knows best.

﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, upon your heart, that you may be among the warners, in clear Arabic speech. And indeed it is in the Scriptures of the former peoples.﴾
