* * *

As for His saying: ﴿upon your heart﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: He said ﴿upon your heart﴾, although He sent it down to him, in order to affirm that this revealed matter is preserved for the Messenger and firmly fixed in his heart, not subject to alteration. Thus the warning issued by him is trusted, and Allah has made clear that this is the purpose. For this reason He said: ﴿that you may be among the warners﴾.

The second: The heart is in reality the one addressed, because it is the locus of discernment and choice, while the other limbs are subservient to it. The evidence for this is the Qur'an, the hadith, and reason. As for the Qur'an, there are verses:

The first: His saying, exalted is He, in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart﴾, and here He said: ﴿The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, upon your heart﴾, and He said: ﴿Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart﴾ [Qaf: 37].

The second: He mentioned that the deserving of recompense is only according to what is in the heart of striving, so He said: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾ [al-Baqarah: 225], and He said: ﴿Their flesh will not reach Allah, nor their blood, but piety from you will reach Him﴾ [al-Hajj: 37]. And piety is in the heart, because He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾ [al-Hujurat: 3], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And what is within the breasts is made apparent﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 10].

The third: His saying, relating of the people of the Fire: ﴿If we had been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze﴾ [al-Mulk: 10]. It is known that reason is in the heart, and hearing is a conduit to it. And He said: ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of those will be questioned﴾ [al-Isra: 36]. It is known that hearing and sight benefit only from what they convey to the heart, so the questioning about them is in reality a questioning about the heart. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾ [Ghafir: 19], and the eyes conceal nothing except what the hearts harbor when gazing at them.

The fourth: His saying: ﴿And He made for you hearing, sight, and hearts; little are you grateful﴾ [al-Sajdah: 9]. He singled out these three for the establishment of proof and for requiring gratitude for them. We have said: hearing and sight have no value except through what they convey to the heart, so that the heart is the judge over them and the one who controls them. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We had established them in what We have not established you in, and We had made for them hearing, sight, and hearts, but their hearing did not avail them, nor their sight, nor their hearts﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 26]. So He made these three the completion of what He had established against them as proof, and the aim of that is the heart, which judges what hearing and sight convey to it.

The fifth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and upon their sight﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7]. So He made the punishment incumbent upon these three, and said: ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand, and they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear﴾ [al-A'raf: 179]. The point of evidence is that He intended the negation of knowledge from them altogether; if knowledge were established in something other than the heart as it is established in the heart, the purpose would not be complete. So these verses and their like all attest together that the heart is the one intended in establishing proof. We have explained that what is mentioned alongside it of hearing and sight is because they are two instruments of the heart in conveying the forms of perceptible and audible things.

As for the hadith, it is what al-Nu'man ibn Bashir related, who said: I heard him, peace be upon him, say: "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart."

As for reason, there are several aspects:

The first: When the heart is overcome by unconsciousness, even if all other limbs were cut off, no awareness of them would arise; and when the heart regains consciousness, it perceives everything that befalls the limbs of afflictions. This indicates that the other limbs follow the heart. This is why, when the heart rejoices or grieves, the state of the limbs changes accordingly, and likewise regarding all the psychological states.

The second: The heart is the source of the motives that prompt the actions issuing from the other limbs. When motives are the origins of actions and their source is the heart, the absolute commander is the heart.

The third: The seat of reason is the heart, and when this is so, the absolute commander is the heart.

As for the first premise, there is dispute about it, for a group of the early scholars held that the seat of reason is the brain. What indicates our view are several aspects:

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not traveled in the land so that they would have hearts with which to understand?﴾ [al-Hajj: 46], and His saying: ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand﴾ [al-A'raf: 179], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart﴾ [Qaf: 37], meaning intellect. He named it "heart" because it is its locus.

The second: He, exalted is He, attributed the opposites of knowledge to the heart, and said: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾ [al-Ahzab: 12]; ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7]; ﴿Our hearts are uncircumcised; rather, Allah has sealed them for their disbelief﴾ [al-Nisa: 155]; ﴿The hypocrites fear that a surah will be sent down about them informing them of what is in their hearts﴾ [al-Tawbah: 64]; ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾ [al-Fath: 11]; ﴿Nay, rather, what they have earned has covered over their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 14]; ﴿Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ [Muhammad: 24]; ﴿Indeed, it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind﴾ [al-Hajj: 46]. These verses indicate that the locus of ignorance and heedlessness is the heart, so the locus of intellect and understanding must also be the heart.

The third: When we examine ourselves, we find our knowledge present in the region of the heart. This is why, when one of us deeply reflects and persists in thought, he senses in his heart constriction and weariness, to the point that it seems he is suffering from it. All of this indicates that the locus of intellect is the heart. Once this is established, it follows that the one addressed by obligation is the heart, because obligation is conditioned upon intellect and understanding.

The fourth: The heart is the first of the organs to form and the last to die, and this has been established by dissection. Moreover, it is situated in the chest, which is the middle of the body, and it is the nature of kings who need attendants to be in the middle of their kingdom, so that retainers surround them from all sides, and they are thus further from calamities.

Those who said that reason is in the brain argued with several matters:

The first: The senses, which are the instruments of perception, lead to the brain and not to the heart.

The second: The nerves, which are the instruments of voluntary movements, extend from the brain and not from the heart.

The third: When a defect strikes the brain, reason becomes disordered.

The fourth: In common usage, whenever someone is described as having little intellect, it is said that he is "light of brain, light of head."

The fifth: Intellect is more noble, so its place is more noble, and the higher is the more noble; that is the brain and not the heart. Therefore, the seat of intellect must be the brain.

The answer to the first: Why should it not be said that the senses transmit their effects to the brain, and then the brain transmits those effects to the heart? Thus the brain is the proximate instrument of the heart, and the senses are distant instruments; the sense serves the brain, and the brain serves the heart. The verification of this is that we perceive from ourselves that when we understand that a certain matter must be done or must be avoided, the limbs move accordingly, and we find that the intellections come from the side of the heart and not from the side of the brain.

The answer to the second: It is not far-fetched that the effect passes from the heart to the brain, and then the brain moves the limbs through the nerves that sprout from it.

The answer to the third: It is not far-fetched that the soundness of the brain is a condition for the heart's influence to reach the rest of the limbs.

The answer to the fourth: That usage arose because the heart's temperament is balanced by what it draws from the brain of its coolness. When the brain suffers a departure from balance, the heart also departs from balance, either by an increase of its heat beyond the required measure or by a decrease of its heat below that measure, and then reason becomes disordered.

The answer to the fifth: If what they said were correct, the seat of intellect would have to be the skull's cavity, and since that is invalid, the falsity of their view is established. And Allah knows best.

Branch: Know that the meanings we have explained as being specific to the hearts are sometimes attributed to the chest (sadr) and at other times to the heart (fu'ad). As for the chest, the evidence is His saying: ﴿And what is within the breasts is made apparent﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 10], His saying: ﴿And that Allah may test what is in your breasts﴾ [Al 'Imran: 154], His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He knows the secrets of the breasts﴾ [al-Anfal: 43], and ﴿Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it﴾ [Al 'Imran: 29]. As for the fu'ad (heart), the evidence is His saying: ﴿And We turn about their hearts and their sight﴾ [al-An'am: 110].

Some people distinguished between the qalb (heart) and the fu'ad, saying: the qalb is the black clot within the fu'ad apart from the flesh and fat surrounding it, and the whole of that is the fu'ad. Others said the qalb and the fu'ad are synonymous terms. Whatever the case, it must be known that within the organ called qalb and fu'ad there is a locus that is in reality the locus of reason and choice, and that the bulk of this organ is subservient to that locus, just as the other limbs are subservient to the heart. For the organ's parts may increase without any increase in the meanings attributed to it, namely reason, joy, and grief, and may decrease without any decrease in those meanings. It is therefore likely that the name "qalb" is the name for the parts in which these meanings truly reside, and the name "fu'ad" is the name for the whole organ. This is the discussion on this subject, and Allah is the granter of success toward what is correct.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 26, verses 194–196 (part 2 of 2):

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿that you may be among the warners﴾, warning (indhar) includes calling to every obligation of knowledge and action, and prohibiting every ugly deed, because both aspects together include fear of punishment.
* * *
As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿in a clear Arabic tongue﴾, the preposition (ba') may be connected to "al-mundhirin" (the warners), so that the meaning is: that you may be among those who warned with this tongue, and they were five: Hud, Salih, Shu'ayb, Isma'il and Muhammad, peace be upon them. Or it may be connected to "nazala" (He sent down), so that the meaning is: He sent it down in the Arabic tongue so that he might warn with it, because if He had sent it down in a non-Arabic (a'jami) tongue, they would have said to him, "What shall we do with what we do not understand?", and warning with it would have been impossible. In this view, sending it down in Arabic, which is your tongue and the tongue of your people, is a sending down upon your heart, because you understand it and your people understand it. Had it been non-Arabic, it would have been sent down upon your hearing and not your heart, because you would hear the jingling of letters whose meanings you do not understand.
* * *
As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed it is in the Scriptures of the former peoples﴾, this may refer to these reports specifically; it may mean the attribute of the Qur'an; it may mean the attribute of Muhammad (ﷺ); and it may mean the aspects of warning, since the mention of all these things has already preceded.

The Discussion Concerning What Allah Mentioned of the Circumstances of Muhammad, peace be upon him

﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, upon your heart, that you may be among the warners, in clear Arabic speech. And indeed it is in the Scriptures of the former peoples.﴾

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, upon your heart, that you may be among the warners, in clear Arabic speech. And indeed it is in the Scriptures of the former peoples.﴾

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, concluded what He had related of the report of the prophets, He mentioned after that what indicates his prophethood, peace and blessings be upon him, and this is from two aspects:

The first: His saying, ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾. This is because, by its eloquence, it is inimitable, so it must be from the Lord of the worlds. Or because it reports past narratives without any instruction at all, so this could only be by revelation from Allah, exalted is He. His saying after it, ﴿And indeed it is in the Scriptures of the former peoples﴾, seems to confirm this possibility. This is because, when he, peace be upon him, related these seven narratives as they exist in the Scriptures of the former peoples without any discrepancy whatsoever, although he had not occupied himself with learning or preparation, this indicates that it is nothing but from Allah, exalted is He. This is the purpose of the verse.

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾, the meaning of "tanzil" (revelation) here is "munazzal" (that which is sent down). Then, it was permissible for the Qur'an and these narratives to be a revelation from Allah, exalted is He, to Muhammad, peace be upon him, without an intermediary; but He said: ﴿The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾. The preposition "bi" in His saying ﴿The Spirit has brought it down with it﴾ and "nuzzila bihi al-ruh" (it was brought down with it by the Spirit), according to both readings, is for transitivity (ta'diyah). The meaning of ﴿nazala bihi al-ruh﴾ is: Allah made the Spirit descend with it upon your heart, that is, He made you understand it and established it in your heart as something that is not forgotten, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We will make you recite, so you will not forget﴾ [al-A'la: 6]. "Al-Ruh al-Amin" (the trustworthy Spirit) is Jibril, peace be upon him. He was called "Ruh" (Spirit) from the aspect that he was created from the Spirit. It was also said: because he is the salvation of creation in matters of religion, so he is like the spirit with which life is sustained. It was also said: because he is entirely spirit, unlike the people, who have a spirit within their bodies. He was called "Amin" (trustworthy) because he is entrusted with what he conveys to the prophets, peace be upon them, and to others.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿upon your heart﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: He said ﴿upon your heart﴾, although He sent it down to him, in order to affirm that this revealed matter is preserved for the Messenger and firmly fixed in his heart, not subject to alteration. Thus the warning issued by him is trusted, and Allah has made clear that this is the purpose. For this reason He said: ﴿that you may be among the warners﴾.

The second: The heart is in reality the one addressed, because it is the locus of discernment and choice, while the other limbs are subservient to it. The evidence for this is the Qur'an, the hadith, and reason. As for the Qur'an, there are verses:

The first: His saying, exalted is He, in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart﴾, and here He said: ﴿The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, upon your heart﴾, and He said: ﴿Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart﴾ [Qaf: 37].

The second: He mentioned that the deserving of recompense is only according to what is in the heart of striving, so He said: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾ [al-Baqarah: 225], and He said: ﴿Their flesh will not reach Allah, nor their blood, but piety from you will reach Him﴾ [al-Hajj: 37]. And piety is in the heart, because He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾ [al-Hujurat: 3], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And what is within the breasts is made apparent﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 10].

The third: His saying, relating of the people of the Fire: ﴿If we had been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze﴾ [al-Mulk: 10]. It is known that reason is in the heart, and hearing is a conduit to it. And He said: ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of those will be questioned﴾ [al-Isra: 36]. It is known that hearing and sight benefit only from what they convey to the heart, so the questioning about them is in reality a questioning about the heart. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾ [Ghafir: 19], and the eyes conceal nothing except what the hearts harbor when gazing at them.

The fourth: His saying: ﴿And He made for you hearing, sight, and hearts; little are you grateful﴾ [al-Sajdah: 9]. He singled out these three for the establishment of proof and for requiring gratitude for them. We have said: hearing and sight have no value except through what they convey to the heart, so that the heart is the judge over them and the one who controls them. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We had established them in what We have not established you in, and We had made for them hearing, sight, and hearts, but their hearing did not avail them, nor their sight, nor their hearts﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 26]. So He made these three the completion of what He had established against them as proof, and the aim of that is the heart, which judges what hearing and sight convey to it.

The fifth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and upon their sight﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7]. So He made the punishment incumbent upon these three, and said: ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand, and they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear﴾ [al-A'raf: 179]. The point of evidence is that He intended the negation of knowledge from them altogether; if knowledge were established in something other than the heart as it is established in the heart, the purpose would not be complete. So these verses and their like all attest together that the heart is the one intended in establishing proof. We have explained that what is mentioned alongside it of hearing and sight is because they are two instruments of the heart in conveying the forms of perceptible and audible things.

As for the hadith, it is what al-Nu'man ibn Bashir related, who said: I heard him, peace be upon him, say: "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart."

As for reason, there are several aspects:

The first: When the heart is overcome by unconsciousness, even if all other limbs were cut off, no awareness of them would arise; and when the heart regains consciousness, it perceives everything that befalls the limbs of afflictions. This indicates that the other limbs follow the heart. This is why, when the heart rejoices or grieves, the state of the limbs changes accordingly, and likewise regarding all the psychological states.

The second: The heart is the source of the motives that prompt the actions issuing from the other limbs. When motives are the origins of actions and their source is the heart, the absolute commander is the heart.

The third: The seat of reason is the heart, and when this is so, the absolute commander is the heart.

As for the first premise, there is dispute about it, for a group of the early scholars held that the seat of reason is the brain. What indicates our view are several aspects:

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not traveled in the land so that they would have hearts with which to understand?﴾ [al-Hajj: 46], and His saying: ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand﴾ [al-A'raf: 179], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart﴾ [Qaf: 37], meaning intellect. He named it "heart" because it is its locus.

The second: He, exalted is He, attributed the opposites of knowledge to the heart, and said: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾ [al-Ahzab: 12]; ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7]; ﴿Our hearts are uncircumcised; rather, Allah has sealed them for their disbelief﴾ [al-Nisa: 155]; ﴿The hypocrites fear that a surah will be sent down about them informing them of what is in their hearts﴾ [al-Tawbah: 64]; ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾ [al-Fath: 11]; ﴿Nay, rather, what they have earned has covered over their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 14]; ﴿Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ [Muhammad: 24]; ﴿Indeed, it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind﴾ [al-Hajj: 46]. These verses indicate that the locus of ignorance and heedlessness is the heart, so the locus of intellect and understanding must also be the heart.

The third: When we examine ourselves, we find our knowledge present in the region of the heart. This is why, when one of us deeply reflects and persists in thought, he senses in his heart constriction and weariness, to the point that it seems he is suffering from it. All of this indicates that the locus of intellect is the heart. Once this is established, it follows that the one addressed by obligation is the heart, because obligation is conditioned upon intellect and understanding.

The fourth: The heart is the first of the organs to form and the last to die, and this has been established by dissection. Moreover, it is situated in the chest, which is the middle of the body, and it is the nature of kings who need attendants to be in the middle of their kingdom, so that retainers surround them from all sides, and they are thus further from calamities.

Those who said that reason is in the brain argued with several matters:

The first: The senses, which are the instruments of perception, lead to the brain and not to the heart.

The second: The nerves, which are the instruments of voluntary movements, extend from the brain and not from the heart.

The third: When a defect strikes the brain, reason becomes disordered.

The fourth: In common usage, whenever someone is described as having little intellect, it is said that he is "light of brain, light of head."

The fifth: Intellect is more noble, so its place is more noble, and the higher is the more noble; that is the brain and not the heart. Therefore, the seat of intellect must be the brain.

The answer to the first: Why should it not be said that the senses transmit their effects to the brain, and then the brain transmits those effects to the heart? Thus the brain is the proximate instrument of the heart, and the senses are distant instruments; the sense serves the brain, and the brain serves the heart. The verification of this is that we perceive from ourselves that when we understand that a certain matter must be done or must be avoided, the limbs move accordingly, and we find that the intellections come from the side of the heart and not from the side of the brain.

The answer to the second: It is not far-fetched that the effect passes from the heart to the brain, and then the brain moves the limbs through the nerves that sprout from it.

The answer to the third: It is not far-fetched that the soundness of the brain is a condition for the heart's influence to reach the rest of the limbs.

The answer to the fourth: That usage arose because the heart's temperament is balanced by what it draws from the brain of its coolness. When the brain suffers a departure from balance, the heart also departs from balance, either by an increase of its heat beyond the required measure or by a decrease of its heat below that measure, and then reason becomes disordered.

The answer to the fifth: If what they said were correct, the seat of intellect would have to be the skull's cavity, and since that is invalid, the falsity of their view is established. And Allah knows best.

Branch: Know that the meanings we have explained as being specific to the hearts are sometimes attributed to the chest (sadr) and at other times to the heart (fu'ad). As for the chest, the evidence is His saying: ﴿And what is within the breasts is made apparent﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 10], His saying: ﴿And that Allah may test what is in your breasts﴾ [Al 'Imran: 154], His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He knows the secrets of the breasts﴾ [al-Anfal: 43], and ﴿Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it﴾ [Al 'Imran: 29]. As for the fu'ad (heart), the evidence is His saying: ﴿And We turn about their hearts and their sight﴾ [al-An'am: 110].

Some people distinguished between the qalb (heart) and the fu'ad, saying: the qalb is the black clot within the fu'ad apart from the flesh and fat surrounding it, and the whole of that is the fu'ad. Others said the qalb and the fu'ad are synonymous terms. Whatever the case, it must be known that within the organ called qalb and fu'ad there is a locus that is in reality the locus of reason and choice, and that the bulk of this organ is subservient to that locus, just as the other limbs are subservient to the heart. For the organ's parts may increase without any increase in the meanings attributed to it, namely reason, joy, and grief, and may decrease without any decrease in those meanings. It is therefore likely that the name "qalb" is the name for the parts in which these meanings truly reside, and the name "fu'ad" is the name for the whole organ. This is the discussion on this subject, and Allah is the granter of success toward what is correct.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 26, verses 197–202:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾ ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs,﴾ ﴿and he had recited it to them, they would not have been believers in it.﴾ ﴿Thus We have inserted it into the hearts of the criminals.﴾ ﴿They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment,﴾ ﴿so it will come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive.﴾

Know that His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾ is intended to mention the second proof of his prophethood (ﷺ) and truthfulness. Its explanation is that a group of the scholars of the Children of Israel embraced Islam and pointed to passages in the Tawrat (Torah) and the Injil (Gospel) in which the Messenger (ﷺ) is mentioned by his attributes and description. The idolaters of Quraysh used to go to the Jews and learn this news from them. This clearly indicates his prophethood, because the agreement of the divine books on his description and attributes decisively proves his prophethood.

Know also that it is read ﴿yakun﴾ with the masculine form, and ﴿ayatan﴾ in the accusative, so that it is its predicate (khabar) and ﴿an ya'lamahu﴾ is the subject (ism). It is also read ﴿takun﴾ with the feminine form, with ﴿ayatun﴾ made the subject and ﴿an ya'lamahu﴾ the predicate. The two readings are not identical, because in the second an indefinite noun is the subject and a definite phrase is the predicate. With the accusative of ﴿ayatan﴾, it is also permissible to make ﴿yakun﴾ feminine, as in His saying: ﴿Then their trial will not be but that they say﴾ [al-An'am: 23].

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs﴾, know that when He, may He be exalted, had shown by the two proofs mentioned the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the truthfulness of his speech, He then showed that these disbelievers are not benefited by proofs or evidences. So He said: ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs﴾, meaning: We sent down this Qur'an upon a man who was an Arab, in a clear Arabic tongue. They heard it, understood it, and recognised its eloquence, and that it is a miracle that cannot be matched by speech like it. To this was added the announcement of the earlier books of God concerning him. Yet they did not believe in him, they denied him, and at one time called him a poet and at another a sorcerer. So if We had sent it down upon some non-Arab who does not speak Arabic well, they would have disbelieved in it as well, and they would have contrived an excuse for their denial.

Then He said: ﴿Thus We have inserted it into the hearts of the criminals﴾, that is: in the same manner of insertion We have inserted it into their hearts. Thus We have established and fixed it in them. Whatever He does with them, there is no way for them to change from their state of denial and rejection. This also serves to console the Messenger (ﷺ), because when the Messenger of God knows their persistence in disbelief, and that the eternal decree has passed concerning it, despair arises in him. As the proverb says: "Despair is one of the two comforts."

**The fourth issue:** His saying ﴿Thus We have inserted it into the hearts of the criminals﴾ indicates that everything is by God's decree and creation. The author of the *Kashshaf* (al-Zamakhshari) said: he meant that this denial became firmly established in their hearts to the utmost degree, so that it became like an innate matter.

The answer is this: either God has done to them something that requires the preponderance of denial over affirmation, or He has not done that to them. If the first is the case, we have already shown in Surah al-An'am that preponderance is not realised unless it reaches the level of necessity (wujub), and then the intended meaning is achieved. If He has done nothing to them that requires preponderance at all, then His saying ﴿Thus We have inserted it﴾ is impossible, just as the flying of a bird, since it has no connection to their disbelief, makes it impossible to attribute disbelief to that flying.

**The fifth issue:** The author of the *Kashshaf* said: If you ask, what is the position of ﴿They will not believe in it﴾ in relation to His saying ﴿We have inserted it into the hearts of the criminals﴾? I say: its position relative to it is that of an elucidating and explaining clause, because it is brought in to explain it and to confirm the denial in their hearts. So it follows what establishes this meaning, namely that they will not cease to deny it until they witness the threat.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 26, verses 210–213:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And the devils have not brought it down.﴾ ﴿It is not befitting for them, nor are they able to do so.﴾ ﴿Indeed, they are removed far from hearing it.﴾ ﴿So do not invoke with Allah another god, lest you be among those punished.﴾

Know that when Allah the Exalted argued for the truthfulness of Muhammad (ﷺ) by the fact that the Qur'an is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds, this is recognized only through its utmost eloquence, and because it contains the stories of earlier peoples without discrepancy, while he (peace be upon him) did not engage in learning or acquiring knowledge. The disbelievers would say: why could this not be from the inspiration of the jinn and devils, like everything that descends upon the soothsayers (kahanah, pl. of kāhin, "soothsayer")? Allah the Exalted answered this by saying that such a thing is not easy for the devils, because they are pelted with meteors and are removed from listening to the speech of the people of the heaven.

Someone might say: the knowledge that the devils are prevented from this is obtained only through the report of the truthful Prophet. So, when we establish that Muhammad (ﷺ) is truthful by the eloquence of the Qur'an and his reports of the unseen, and it is not possible to establish that eloquence and reports of the unseen are a miracle except when it is established that the devils are prevented from this, a circular argument follows, and it is invalid. Its answer: we do not accept that the knowledge that the devils are prevented from this is obtained only from the words of the Prophet. This is because we know by necessity that concern for the friend is stronger than concern for the enemy, and we know by necessity that Muhammad (ﷺ) used to curse the devils and command people to curse them. So if this unseen knowledge had come only from the inspiration of the devils, the disbelievers would have been more entitled to acquire such knowledge, and their capacity to achieve the like of it would have been more fitting. Since this is not the case, we know that the devils are prevented from this, and that they are removed from attaining the unseen.

Then, when Allah the Exalted mentioned this answer, He began addressing the Messenger (ﷺ), saying: ﴿So do not invoke with Allah another god﴾. In reality this is an address to others, because it is the way of the wise, when he wishes to emphasize an address to others, to direct it to the leaders outwardly, even though the intended audience is the followers. Also, Allah the Exalted wished to follow it with what is fitting for this, and for this reason He singled him out for the address.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 26, verses 214–220:

﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk﴾ ﴿and lower your wing to the believers who follow you﴾ ﴿but if they disobey you, say: "I am innocent of what you do"﴾ ﴿and put your trust in the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ ﴿who sees you when you stand﴾ ﴿and your movements among those who prostrate﴾ ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾.

Know that when He, glorified is He, had thoroughly consoled His Messenger first, then established the proof for his prophethood second, then raised the question of the deniers and answered it third, He then commanded him, after that, with what relates to the matter of conveying the message and the mission. Here there are three matters:

The first: His saying, ﴿And warn your closest kinsfolk﴾. This is because He, exalted is He, began with the Messenger, threatening him if he called upon another god along with God. Then He commanded him to call the nearest, then the next nearest. This is because if he is strict with himself first, and then with the nearest, then the next nearest, no one can find any fault in him at all, his words will be more beneficial and his speech more effective. It is narrated that: "When this verse was revealed, he (ﷺ) ascended al-Safa and called out to the nearest and then the next nearest, saying: 'O Banu Hashim! O Banu 'Abd Manaf! O 'Abbas, uncle of Muhammad! O Safiyyah, aunt of Muhammad! Indeed, I cannot avail you anything against God. Ask me for whatever wealth you wish.'" It is also narrated that: "He gathered the sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib, who were forty men at that time, over the leg of a sheep and a bowl of milk. Each man among them would eat a young camel and drink a large cup. They ate and drank, and then he said: 'O sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib, if I told you that there were horses at the foot of this mountain, would you believe me?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Indeed, I am a warner to you before a severe punishment.'"

The second: His saying, ﴿and lower your wing﴾. Know that when a bird wants to descend to alight, it folds and lowers its wing, and when it wants to rise for flight, it raises its wing. So He made the lowering of the wing at the time of descent a metaphor for humility and gentleness of manner. If it is said: "Those who follow the Messenger are the believers, and vice versa, so why did He say: ﴿to the believers who follow you﴾?" The answer: We do not concede that those who follow the Messenger are the believers, for many of them used to follow him because of kinship and lineage, not because of religion.

As for His saying: ﴿but if they disobey you, say: "I am innocent of what you do"﴾, its meaning is clear. Al-Jubba'i said: This indicates that he, peace be upon him, was innocent of their disobedience, and this necessitates that God, exalted is He, is also innocent of their deeds, just as the Messenger is; otherwise He would be opposing God, just as if he were pleased with one whom God is angry with, he would be the same. And if God, exalted is He, is innocent of their deeds, how can He be their doer and the one who wills them? The answer: He, exalted is He, is innocent of acts of disobedience in the sense that He did not command them but rather forbade them. As for in the sense that He does not will them, we do not concede that. The proof of this is that He knew they would occur, and whatever is known to occur is necessarily going to occur; otherwise His knowledge would turn into ignorance, which is impossible, and what leads to an impossibility is impossible. And He knew that what necessarily occurs is not willed to not occur. Thus what we have said is established.

The third: His saying: ﴿and put your trust﴾. Tawakkul (trust in God) is an expression for a person entrusting his affair to one who controls his affair and is able to benefit or harm him. His saying: ﴿in the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ means: in the One who subdues your enemies by His might and grants you victory over them by His mercy. Then He followed His being Merciful toward His Messenger with what is like the cause of that mercy, namely his standing and his movements among those who prostrate. Regarding this there are several aspects:

First: What is meant is what he used to do in the depth of the night, of standing for tahajjud (night prayer) and turning over in examining the states of those who strive, in order to become aware of their secrets. It is related that when the obligation of night prayer was abrogated (naskh), he went around the houses of his companions that night to see what they were doing, out of his eagerness for whatever acts of obedience could be found among them. He found them like the hives of wasps, due to the murmuring of their remembrance of God, exalted is He, which he heard from them. What is meant by "those who prostrate" is those who pray.

Second: The meaning is: He sees you when you stand for the prayer leading the people in congregation, and His "turning" you among those who prostrate is His directing you among them through your standing, bowing, prostration and sitting, since you were their imam.

Third: That your condition is not hidden from Him whenever you stand and turn among those who prostrate, in the sufficiency of the affairs of the religion.

Fourth: What is meant is the turning of his sight toward those who pray behind him, from his saying (ﷺ): "Complete the bowing and the prostration, for by God, I see you from behind me."

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing﴾, meaning: of what you say; ﴿the All-Knowing﴾, meaning: of what you intend and do. This indicates that His being All-Hearing is a matter distinct from His knowledge of things heard; otherwise the word "All-Knowing" would have conveyed its meaning. Know that it has been read as "wa-nuqallibuka" (and We turn you).

Know that the Rafidah (Rafidites) held that the fathers of the Prophet (ﷺ) were believers, and they clung to this verse and to a report in this matter. As for the verse, they said: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and your movements among those who prostrate﴾ admits the aspects you have mentioned, and it may also mean that God, exalted is He, transferred his spirit from one prostrating person to another, as we say. And when it admits all these aspects, it is necessary to apply the verse to all of them, since there is no contradiction and no preference. As for the report, it is his saying, peace be upon him: "I was never moved from the loins of the pure men to the wombs of the pure women," and everyone who was a disbeliever is impure, due to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are impure﴾ [al-Tawbah: 28]. They said: If you cling, to refute this doctrine, to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾ [al-An'am: 74], we say: The answer to this is that the word "father" may be applied to an uncle, as the sons of Jacob said to him: ﴿We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael and Isaac﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133]. They called Ishmael a "father" to him, although he was his uncle. And he, peace be upon him, said: "Return my father to me," meaning al-'Abbas. It is also possible that the one who took idols was the father of his mother, for this too may be called "father." Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 26, verses 221–223:

﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?﴾ ﴿They descend upon every lying sinner.﴾ ﴿They lend their ear, and most of them are liars.﴾

Page 150

Know that God, exalted is He, repeated the earlier doubt and answered it in two ways:

The first: His saying, ﴿They descend upon every lying sinner.﴾ This is what we established earlier, namely that the disbelievers were being called to obey the devil, while Muhammad, peace be upon him, was calling to cursing the devil and disassociating from him.

The second: His saying, ﴿They lend their ear, and most of them are liars.﴾ The meaning is that they were measuring the state of the Prophet ﷺ by the state of all the other soothsayers (kahana). So it is as if it were said to them: If the matter is as you have claimed, then just as the soothsayers in general are characterised by lying, the state of the Messenger ﷺ must likewise be so. But since nothing appeared in the Messenger's ﷺ reports about unseen matters except truthfulness, we know that his condition is contrary to the condition of the soothsayers.

Then, the exegetes (mufassirun) mentioned several views regarding the verse:

One of them: that the ones meant are the devils. It is related that before they were barred by being pelted with meteors (rajm), they would eavesdrop on the higher assembly (al-mala' al-a'la, the angels), snatching some of what they said about the unseen matters they had learned, and then they would inspire it to their associates. ﴿And most of them are liars﴾ in what they inspire to them, because they make them hear what they did not hear.

The second: they lend to their associates the ear, meaning what is heard from the angels.

The third: the lying sinners lend their ear to the devils, and so they convey their revelation to them.

The fourth: they convey to people what they hear from the devils, and most lying sinners are liars, inventing against the devils what they did not reveal to them.

If you ask: what is the grammatical position (mahall) of ﴿yulqun﴾ (they lend)? I say: it may be in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning "they descend while lending the ear." It may be in the genitive position as an adjective (sifa) of "kulli affakin" (every lying one), because it has the sense of a plural. And it may have no position at all, by being a new resumptive clause (isti'naf), as if someone had said: Why do they descend upon the lying sinners? So it was answered: they do such-and-such. If you ask: how? He said: ﴿and most of them are liars﴾, after He had already decided that each of them is a lying sinner? I say: the "affakun" are those who frequently lie, not those who speak only falsehood. So He intended that few of these lying sinners are truthful in what they relate about the jinn, and most of them fabricate against them.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 26, verses 224–227:**

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And the poets, the erring follow them.﴾ ﴿Do you not see that they wander in every valley?﴾ ﴿And that they say what they do not do?﴾ ﴿Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, remember Allah often, and defend themselves after they have been wronged. And those who wronged will know what return they will be returned to.﴾

Know that when the disbelievers said, "Why is it not possible to say that the devils descend upon Muhammad with the Qur'an, just as they descend with soothsaying (kahana, the practice of foretelling hidden matters) upon the soothsayers (kahana, pl. of kahin), and with poetry upon the poets?" Then He, glorified is He, made a distinction between Muhammad ﷺ and the soothsayers. Here He mentioned what indicates the distinction between him, peace be upon him, and the poets. That is that "the poets, the erring follow them," meaning the misguided. Then He clarified that error with two matters:

The first: ﴿that they wander in every valley﴾, and what is meant by it is the various paths, as when you say, "I am in one valley and you are in another." That is because they sometimes praise a thing after they have condemned it, and vice versa, and they sometimes glorify it after they had belittled it, and vice versa. This indicates that they do not seek truth or sincerity in their poetry, unlike the matter of Muhammad ﷺ, for from the beginning of his affair to its end he remained upon one path, which is calling to Allah, the Exalted, encouraging the Hereafter, and turning away from this world.

[Page 151]
